name: New Mexico
overview: New Mexico's big-game draw is a pure random draw with no preference or bonus points: each application gets a random sequence number and the system tries the applicant's 1st, 2nd, then 3rd hunt choice (deer and elk applicants may add a 4th-choice quadrant filled in a second drawing). State law sets quotas for each hunt: a minimum of 84% of licenses to residents, 10% to residents or nonresidents applying with a New Mexico registered outfitter, and 6% to nonresidents without an outfitter; antlerless elk and WMA-only hunts are 100% resident. For 2026 the big-game application deadline was March 18 (results April 22) and the bear/turkey draw-permit deadline was February 11 (results February 18). The agency, formerly the Department of Game and Fish, is now the New Mexico Department of Wildlife (NMDOW).

species.drawSystemSummary: Random draw with no preference or bonus points: each application gets a random sequence number and the system tries the 1st, 2nd, then 3rd hunt choice. Statutory quotas per hunt: at least 84% resident, 10% to residents or nonresidents applying with a NM registered outfitter, 6% nonresidents without an outfitter. Antlerless elk and WMA-only hunts are 100% resident; deer and elk applicants may add a 4th-choice quadrant filled in a second drawing.
species.residentNote: Residents receive a minimum of 84% of licenses in each hunt, and 100% of antlerless (A) and WMA-only elk licenses.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents draw from the 6% pool (or the 10% outfitter pool if applying with a NM registered outfitter). NMDOW notes it is extremely unlikely for a nonresident to draw a hunt code with 12 or fewer licenses, or an outfitted applicant one with six or fewer. Nonresidents are ineligible for antlerless elk and WMA hunts.
species.otcSummary: No public-land OTC elk licenses. Private-land elk hunting uses landowner-issued ranch-only or unit-wide authorizations with a Private-Land Elk License (2026-27 booklet page 73); these are outside the public draw and its odds reports.

species.drawSystemSummary: Bear hunting is mainly over the counter: an OTC Bear License is valid in open bear management zones until each zone's harvest limit is reached. A separate random draw issues bear draw permits for a few special areas (WMAs, Valle Vidal, Sugarite Canyon State Park); one hunter per application.
species.residentNote: Only New Mexico residents may apply for WMA bear draw permits.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may buy the OTC Bear License and apply for non-WMA bear draw permits (Valle Vidal, Unit 2 youth, Sugarite Canyon).
species.otcSummary: OTC Bear License valid statewide in open zones during zone seasons (bow-only Sept. 1-24 in most zones; any legal sporting arm periods vary by zone). Zones close when harvest limits are reached. Draw permits must also be validated with the OTC Bear License.

coverage.notes: Hunt codes per draw year: 2022: 313, 2023: 322, 2024: 322, 2025: 322, 2026: 322. Big-game complete reports 2022-2026. 2024-2026 first-choice total drawn = resident + nonresident + outfitter first-choice drawn (sum of published pool figures). 2022 all-choice applicants = 1st+2nd+3rd (the 2022 report prints no total column). Cross-check: 2022 elk section Totals row matches the sum of hunts in every column except resident all-choice drawn (hunts sum to 19,853; agency Totals row prints 19,854). Source: NMDOW/NMDGF drawing odds reports (draw years = report years). Each hunt has a choice=first row (1st-choice applicants and licenses drawn on 1st choice) and a choice=all row (1st+2nd+3rd-choice applicants and all licenses drawn). resident = resident pool; nonresident = nonresident pool without an outfitter; the outfitter pool (residents or nonresidents with a NM registered outfitter) is given in each row's note; total = all pools. total.quota = licenses offered in the hunt. oddsPct is computed (drawn / applicants), not published. No points exist, so no byPoints/minPoints. Cross-check: for 2023-2026 the agency's separate Summary Report matches the Complete Report's pre-draw counts for every hunt and its pool drawn counts for every hunt except 2023 ANT-3-155 (see pronghorn notes). All-choice odds overstate the real chance because each application can draw only one hunt; choice=all drawn counts exclude licenses awarded to 4th-choice (any-hunt quadrant) applicants, which are listed in the row note. Season dates (seasonDates/seasonRanges) for the 2026 rows come from the hunt tables of the 2026-2027 Hunting Rules and Information booklet (seasonSourceId d-nm-rib-2026), written by seasons_parse.py.
